findings.text: §8 requires the adapter to compare "the vector the operator already carries with the resolution it is about to install" and asserts they "agree exactly", but the operator built at `benchmarks/diiid_forward_gs_match.py:1356` carries the 19 shipped channels only, while `resolve_diiid_currents` (`nova/imas/diiid_current.py:191`) appends the five circuit-driven conductors ECOILB, E567UP, E567DN, E89UP, E89DN to the 24-current resolution that the adapter installs, so an equality over the two vectors raises on every legitimate call and the section states no comparison domain; a worker either implements a check that reddens the unpatched frame-137D run its own done-when (2) requires to pass, or silently narrows the check to a prefix the plan never names

findings.reason: the corrected arm's meaning is the plan's whole claim, and as stated a later reader would take an arm the evidence calls implausible as the coil-field measurement, so the section must state which arm the implausible vector yields or that the corrected arm is a bound rather than a correction.
findings.text: §9 re-solves the cohort "with the fitted correction" and re-banks those offsets as the corrected arm, but the cited record `docs/evidence/fragments/diiid-vertical-force-balance/diiid-xpoint-coil-correction.html` marks the very fit it quotes (F1A −177.235 to −231.293 kA·turn) as implausible for five of nineteen conductors (30.5 to 1465.2 percent of the coil's own current) and states it does not reproduce the published attribution (F1A +54.06/+52.14 against −2.51/−0.27 kA·turn), leaving a common-mode response or external-field error unidentified; the section would bank that vector as the corrected-current result without carrying its implausibility verdict

findings.reason: the node must either supply the corrected vector or re-fit it, and with the named record unresolvable the plan's equality check "the corrected vector its inputs name" has no durable input to compare against.
findings.text: §9 names `current-inputs.json` as the record of the corrected conductor vector, but neither cited location holds it: `scripts/prototypes/diiid_xpoint_coil_correction/` lists batch.py, conductor_correction.py, fit.py, job.sh, measure.py, probe_applied.py, probe_external.py, render.py, summarize.py, test_conductor_correction.py, and `docs/figures/diiid-xpoint-coil-correction/` holds two window JSON files and two SVGs; a repository-wide search finds the filename only in prose in the two evidence fragments and the plan itself, against the fragment's own statement that "the earlier run's working directories have since been retired from the run store"

findings.reason: without a control that reddens when the corrected arm equals the measured arm, the node's record cannot distinguish a correction that reached the solve from the instrument fault it was created to repair.
findings.text: §9's done-when declares no negative control: its three clauses are a solve, a tabulation, and a prototype test pass, and none of them can fail on the failure the plan itself records, where the corrected arm was bit-identical to the measured arm because the correction never reached the solve; a re-run in which the corpus-column patch again fails to move the state would satisfy every clause
